Core doctrine: an uncertain provider side effect is TERMINAL until proven; never a second create; live GET readback is the only completion truth; two drivers must never race one episode.

LANE A: PUBLISH-SAFETY FIXES (the never-create-twice + truth-source set).

OWNERSHIP: you own ONLY: server/pipeline/orchestrator.py, server/pipeline/publish_readback.py, server/pipeline/zernio.py, tests/test_publish_drain.py, tests/test_publish_orchestrator_resume_fanout.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py, tests/test_publish_readback.py, tests/test_zernio.py. Never modify anything else.

FINDINGS (each: fix + proving test):
1. HIGH orchestrator.py:4251 + :4502 (two sites) - YouTube main and Shorts upload exceptions are not classified before retry: a successful insert with lost response is retryable and can re-insert. Fix: wrap both insert boundaries in ambiguity classification - an exception AFTER the request may have created media: if no provider ID is known, unit -> terminal_ambiguous + review packet (readback/search is the resolution path, never re-insert); only pre-request failures (connection refused before send, auth) are retryable. Persist any session URI/provider ID the moment it is known.
2. HIGH publish_readback.py:252 - ambiguous adoption returns a verdict without persisting state. Fix: adopt_prestaged persists unit state terminal_ambiguous into the episode's publish_units atomically before returning, so a fresh driver call cannot re-create.
3. HIGH zernio.py:729 - posts:create timeouts/nonzero exits/invalid responses become ordinary retryable failures though Zernio may have accepted the request. Fix: same ambiguity doctrine - a create whose acknowledgement is lost = terminal_ambiguous for that post identity + review; resolution reconciles against provider listing (read-only) when available, else stays terminal; only pre-send failures retry.
4. HIGH orchestrator.py:4709 - completion refresh uses receipt-backed fake clients instead of live GET readback. Fix: _refresh_publish_verification must construct the REAL read clients (Transistor/YouTube/site fetch) by default; receipts are inputs for WHICH IDs to read, never substitutes for reading; the injectable seams stay for tests only (default=None -> real).
5. HIGH orchestrator.py:815 - a readback ERROR restores prior verification that may still satisfy the freshness window, so failed GET = fresh-green. Fix: a current readback error for provider X invalidates X's freshness (error recorded with timestamp; completion sees X as NOT fresh); other providers' observations unaffected.
6. HIGH orchestrator.py:5865 - drain and daily cron call handle_publish with no shared claim: concurrent drivers duplicate fanout/clobber receipts. Fix: per-episode publish claim (lock file or claimed_by+expiry in episode.json written atomically with O_EXCL semantics) acquired by BOTH handle_daily_cron's publish path and handle_publish_drain; contested claim = skip with note; stale claim (expiry passed) reclaimable; releasing writes back merged state, never overwrites newer receipts (re-read before final persist).
7. HIGH orchestrator.py:960 - no production path creates a complete canonical publish_expectation for fresh episodes, so side effects can run then completion stalls forever. Fix: expectation is materialized at publish-queue time (calendar assignment / preflight authorization) from episode number, title slug, site URL pattern, show-notes hash, approved clips - BEFORE any provider unit may execute; a missing expectation blocks unit execution (fail closed pre-side-effect, not post).
8. HIGH orchestrator.py:179 - recovery adoption accepts generic not_applicable receipts + any truthy waiver as proof. Fix: adoption proof requires the SPECIFIC gate receipts the standard path demands for that artifact class (transfer + bumper when assembled media exists); waiver must be an explicit structured owner waiver {waived_by, date, reason, scope} - a bare truthy value is invalid; generic not_applicable only for gates inapplicable by construction with recorded reason.
9. MED orchestrator.py:4831 - completed Zernio units are passed back into create_scheduled_posts; receipt loss/account change can mint a new identity for the same unit. Fix: filter completed units out before batch construction; identity comes only from the stored per-post identities.

TESTS: response-loss-after-insert (main + short) -> terminal, zero second inserts; ambiguous adoption persists before return (crash-sim then fresh driver call cannot create); zernio ack-loss -> terminal + no duplicate on drain; refresh uses real clients by default (assert fake-receipt substitution gone via constructor capture); readback error -> provider not fresh -> completion refuses; concurrent drivers (two sequential interleaved calls simulating race) -> single fanout, no receipt loss; fresh episode without expectation cannot execute units + expectation materialized at queue time enables them; unstructured waiver rejected; completed units excluded from batches. ALL existing tests green (list contract updates).

HOW TO RUN: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest tests/test_publish_drain.py tests/test_publish_orchestrator_resume_fanout.py tests/test_orchestrator.py tests/test_publish_readback.py tests/test_zernio.py -q -p no:cacheprovider

OUTPUT CONTRACT: uncommitted changes + ./fix-summary.md ('# Fix Summary','## Summary','## Files Changed','## Verification','## Assumptions', <800 words) mapping each finding to fix + test.

FINDINGS:
1. HIGH app.py:1410 - an existing webhook path still performs direct HubSpot writes outside the gateway lease; the stricter lease enforcement now RAISES during webhook processing, leaving externally completed work without matching CRM state. Fix: route that write through outbound.hubspot_property_patch (the gateway path) preserving the webhook's semantics; the webhook must never 500 on a lease refusal - record + review-queue + 200 with a noted degraded outcome (the external work already happened; CRM catch-up is reconcilable, not a request failure).
2. MED manifest_sync.py:97 - caller-supplied now is embedded into every observation BEFORE diffing, so unchanged manifests hash differently and write every cycle. Fix: diff over content-only canonical form (timestamps excluded); timestamps attach only to the write receipt when a real delta exists; no-op cycles produce zero dispatches (prove with two consecutive syncs).
3. MED publish_reconcile.py:211 - reconciliation reads only publish_expectation while the legacy publish_expected migration lives inside handle_publish, so legacy public episodes reconciled first are falsely incomplete. Fix: extract the migration read into a shared helper (in publish_reconcile.py or a small shared location within your ownership) used by BOTH paths; reconcile of a legacy-keyed episode reads the migrated object identically.

TESTS: webhook path with lease refused -> 200 + review entry + no direct client call (dispatch-capture); two consecutive unchanged syncs -> zero writes; changed field -> one write; legacy-keyed episode reconciles complete. ALL existing tests green.
